title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.29807v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents can write programs that carry out a task without calling a model at every step, so the task runs fast and its logic stays open to inspection. Agents improve these programs by running them, studying their failures, and revising the code, a form of recursive self-improvement (RSI). We ask whether this process also yields runtime checks that can be trusted. In five task domains, with up to seven author models, agents bring their programs to high scores. Yet when the environment changes, the checks they were told to write stay silent on half or more of the resulting failures in four domains. These failures can be detected and repaired: a monitor built from records of normal runs catches most of them in three domains, and the same agents usually repair them once called. translated_title: 对可修复的失败视而不见：自我改进智能体中的检测缺口
translated_abstract: AI智能体能够编写无需在每一步都调用模型的程序来执行任务，从而使任务运行快速且逻辑透明可审查。智能体通过运行程序、分析失败原因并修改代码来改进这些程序，这是一种递归自我改进（RSI）的形式。我们探究这一过程是否也能产生可信的运行时检查。在五个任务领域中，使用多达七个编写代码的模型，智能体能够将其程序提升至高分。然而当环境发生变化时，在四个领域中，它们被要求编写的检查机制对一半甚至更多的由此产生的失败保持沉默。这些失败实际上是可以被检测和修复的：基于正常运行记录构建的监视器在三个领域中捕获了其中大部分失败，而且一旦被提醒，同样的智能体通常能够修复这些问题。这些检查机制没有审查那些能够揭示失败的记录关系，而当最强的智能体被告知其检查存在遗漏时，它编写的检查便能捕获大部分失败。
tldr: 研究发现自我改进智能体能写出高分程序，但其自建的运行时检查在环境变化后对一半以上的失败视而不见，而这些失败其实可通过正常运行记录检测并由智能体自身修复。
en_tdlr: Self-improving AI agents can optimize programs to high scores, but their self-written runtime checks miss half or more of the failures arising from environmental shifts, even though these failures are detectable from normal run records and fixable by the agents themselves once alerted.
